rule_of_thumb: agente precisa ler para saber o que é verdade → docs/ · resultado de olhar o projeto → reports/ · ainda sendo decidido ou mostrado → design/ · não é texto para gente → data/

screenshots.rule: screenshot: dado → data/raw/<assunto>/ · referência de como deve ser → design/references/<assunto>/ · evidência de UAT ou prova de entrega → reports/evidence/<TASK-ID>/ · nome: <TASK-ID|assunto>-<viewport|origem>-AAAA-MM-DD.<ext> · captura do agente entra no git só quando uma task a cita; dado sensível fica fora do git, como em data/raw

sdd.rule: cada feature tem a sua pasta docs/specs/features/Fxx-slug/ com spec.md, plan.md e tasks.md (S-63, grafo de requisitos); docs/specs/milestones/<id>/ é histórico congelado; spec, plan e tasks planos em docs/specs/ são o modelo anterior, aceito até o refresh do projeto

name_decides.rule: o nome decide a casa em qualquer pasta de artefato (raiz, design/, reports/; src/ e tests/ ficam fora — código pode ter 'proposal' no nome): proposta é <assunto>-proposal.<ext> (html, png, md, pdf...) e mora em design/proposals/

diagram_themes.rule: todo diagrama desenhado numa conversa mora num tema: design/diagrams/<tema>/AAAA-MM-DD-HHMM-<name>.png (+ o .svg fonte ao lado); o diagrama de um épico pode ir na subpasta do épico dentro do tema, design/diagrams/<tema>/ep-NN/ (decisão do MJRP, 2026-10-09 18:49: muitos diagramas por épico). Nenhuma outra subpasta. O tema é o assunto, não a fase do PDLC (um diagrama atravessa fases); a fase vai na linha do diagrama no folder-index.md do tema. Tema novo entra aqui, no harness, com o OK do MJRP. Quem gera o caminho certo é o render_diagram.js (--theme, --name, --epic). O diagrama gerado em código também mora aqui (MJRP, 2026-11-02 11:38, F160): o carimbo do nome é o do nascimento e fica; o gerador reescreve o mesmo arquivo, o histórico é o do git, e o SVG basta quando nada lê um PNG.

_deletion_classes: ADR-0023 (F74): the four classes of a path - 1 insubstituível, 2 versionado, 3 derivado, 4 rotativo - are decided by `_pathclass.classify`, which reads these three sections from the rules file of the PROJECT THAT CONTAINS THE PATH (the global entries, from the file beside `_pathclass.py`). Sections are append-only (VT-05); a missing section is an empty list. An entry is {glob, owner, why}; `glob` is relative to the project root in `project`, absolute in `global` (`$TMPDIR` and `~` are expanded). `*` and `?` do not cross a `/`, a segment `**` is any number of folders, a trailing `/` means folders only, and a glob that matches a folder covers everything under it. Linked worktrees are NOT listed: four git tests decide them (the ancestor of main, a clean status, no ignored file outside `derived`, no lock). The F75 daily backup reads `derived.project` for what it leaves out of the copy.

derived._about: class 3: not versioned and regenerable - whoever creates it, deletes it (`_safe.py discard`). Never copied into `_backups/`.

released_copies._about: F84 (UAT-367). A stamped copy in a worktree's `_backups/` (class 4) does not keep a MERGED, clean worktree from leaving when its `source` is listed here AND the copy's content is already in the history of `main` at that path (the judge checks the blob; a copy of an uncommitted hand edit stays). Only generated files that git versions belong here. Nothing is deleted by this list: it only tells the judge of a worktree what the copy protected.

project.why: generated from the disk + structure.yml and versioned; every committed version is in git, so a stamped copy of one is redundant

rewritten_traces._about: F207 (UAT-527). A TRACKED file a tool rewrites in place on each run (the doctor's trace, the build of a branch older than F57, the Next build's `next-env.d.ts`, a `_backups/` a project versions). In a MERGED worktree, an unstaged rewrite of one (a ` M` or ` D` in `git status`), and an untracked file a `derived` glob covers, do not keep it: `_pathclass.judge_worktree` judges the worktree as if they were gone, and `_safe.release_worktree` makes it so before the removal - the tracked one by `_safe.restore` (the edit copied into the MAIN checkout's `_backups/`), the untracked derived one by the discard of class 3. Nothing else changes: a staged change, an edit to any other file, and `classify` (the deletion guard, the main checkout) still see class 1.

budgets._about: ADR-0023 § 3 (ceilings decided by the agent under the MJRP's delegation, log 2026-10-26 01:08, revisable). The doctor's W18 measures each entry and WARNS above the ceiling (an error would take a 13th slot of ADR-0002, which belongs to W13). An entry: id, what it measures (`glob`, or `kind`), the ceiling (`max_gb`, `max_files`, `max_days`, `max_count`, `max_growth`), `owner` (who cleans) and `when`. A path the doctor cannot see from where it runs is a 'não avaliável' note, never 0 GB.
